newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong fetes world press with T-shirts, caps.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong fetes world press with T-shirts, caps.

text.p: The ranks of the world press corps descending on Hong Kong for the handover of the British Colony to China have already enjoyed an early scoop -- a bumper bag of goodies in their press packs.

The journalists, many of whom are hardened hacks equally at home in the world's trouble spots, are being showered with freebies including handover T-shirts, camera film, CD Roms, baseball caps and watches.
At least 8,000 journalists from around the world are expected to be in Hong Kong to document the return of the British colony to China on July 1.
One Hong Kong newspaper put the value of the kit, which consists of 16 separate items and comes in a smart black carrying case, at HK$1,000 ($129).

There has even been talk in press circles that, with a mere eight days before the end of British rule, a few journalists have shown almost as much interest in getting their Hong Kong 1997 year book signed by outgoing colonial governor Chris Patten as in raising last-minute handover-related questions.
A year book bearing the autograph of the last British governor will undoubtedly become a collector's piece as the vestiges of colonialism fade away.
